fixes.explanation: True, friend. The verse says "…the houses had not yet been rebuilt." (Nehemiah 7:4). The same verse says "Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it…" So there's a finished wall and a lot of open room, but the homes aren't back yet.
That's the one. The verse says "…the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were appointed." (Nehemiah 7:1). Doors need somebody standing by them, or they're just fancy wood.

Builders are a fair guess in a story about a wall, so I get why this one sounds right. But the verse names the ones appointed as "…the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites…" (Nehemiah 7:1). The builders aren't on that list.

I see why this one's tempting, since most people open up early. But the text says the opposite. Nehemiah tells them, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot." (Nehemiah 7:3). So the gates wait for the sun to get hot, not for first light.

False is right. Nehemiah says, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot." (Nehemiah 7:3). He adds, "While the guards are on duty, keep the doors shut and securely fastened." So the gates wait for the heat of the day, not first light.

The Tekoites did work on the wall (Nehemiah 3:5), so I see why their name came to mind. But this verse picks someone else. Nehemiah says, "…appoint the residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some at their own homes." (Nehemiah 7:3).
That's it. The verse says, "Now the city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it…" (Nehemiah 7:4). Lots of room, few people.

Counting money is a very human thing to do, I'll admit. But the text says Nehemiah's God put it into his heart to assemble the people "…to be enrolled by genealogy." (Nehemiah 7:5). That's about family lines, not coins.

Trade sounds like a good way to get a young city going. But that isn't what the verse says. God put it into Nehemiah's heart to assemble the people "…to be enrolled by genealogy." (Nehemiah 7:5). That's about family lines.

The Law of Moses matters a lot, so I see why you'd pick it. But here Nehemiah says, "I found the genealogical register of those who had first returned…" (Nehemiah 7:5). It's a family list, not the Law.

False is right. The text says the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants and the rest of the Israelites "…settled in their own towns." (Nehemiah 7:73). They didn't all move inside Jerusalem's walls.
